rows.focus: Meta-analysis of nine dementia trials found cannabinoids did not improve agitation, neuropsychiatric symptoms, or cognition; somnolence was increased.
rows.evidence_boundary: Moderate-to-low certainty, heterogeneous trials; no class-wide efficacy signal.

rows.focus: Systematic review of five RCTs found cannabinoid effects varied strongly by indication and formulation; oral CBD did not help acute low back pain, while THC+CBD and a standardized extract showed signals in specific conditions.
rows.evidence_boundary: Formulation-, route-, and indication-specific findings do not support a class-wide effect.

rows.focus: Review of newer antiseizure medications found substantial agent-specific renal/hepatic pharmacokinetic differences; cannabidiol was among agents less affected by renal decline.
rows.evidence_boundary: Prescription-drug PK review; cannabidiol findings apply to labeled antiseizure-medication use, not general supplement dosing.

rows.focus: Systematic review of 49 rodent studies found THC generally reduced affiliative social behavior in wild-type rodents, with model-, dose-, sex-, and timing-dependent effects.
rows.evidence_boundary: Rodent evidence with reporting limitations cannot be generalized directly to humans.

rows.focus: Four-week canine osteoarthritis study found highly variable CBD exposure and no statistically significant major PK interaction with carprofen, though coadministration signals warrant further study.
rows.evidence_boundary: Veterinary pharmacokinetics; human interaction magnitude cannot be inferred.

rows.focus: CBD/epirubicin-loaded hydroxyapatite nanocarrier improved membrane interaction and ovarian-cancer-cell cytotoxicity in laboratory models.
rows.evidence_boundary: Nanocarrier and cell-culture evidence is preclinical and not evidence for CBD cancer treatment in humans.

rows.focus: EFSA novel-food opinion on ≥98% CBD concluded safety could not be established because key identity, toxicology, reproductive/developmental, and human data gaps were not resolved.
rows.evidence_boundary: Regulatory safety conclusion is specific to the assessed novel-food dossier and proposed use conditions.

rows.focus: EFSA novel-food opinion on a Cannabis sativa extract containing CBD and other cannabinoids concluded safety could not be established because requested data gaps remained unresolved.
rows.evidence_boundary: Regulatory safety conclusion is product/dossier-specific and should not be generalized to all cannabis extracts.

rows.focus: Multicenter retrospective adult epilepsy cohort reported ≥50% seizure reduction in roughly 46% at 12 months, with adverse events common but mostly mild.
rows.evidence_boundary: Retrospective observational data cannot isolate CBD's independent treatment effect; controlled prospective studies are needed.

rows.focus: Systematic review/meta-analysis of CoQ10 in athletes found no robust overall ergogenic or physiological benefit; a favorable oxidative-stress sensitivity signal was fragile and heterogeneous.
rows.evidence_boundary: Small studies and heterogeneity limit confidence; pooled performance outcomes were largely neutral.

rows.focus: Ten-week randomized dietary intervention found moderate pasture-raised red meat maintained plasma DPA relative to a vegetarian PBMA pattern without detectable differences in cardiometabolic biomarkers.
rows.evidence_boundary: Whole-diet comparison cannot be interpreted as an isolated omega-3 supplementation effect.

rows.focus: Randomized double-blind trial found ubiquinone, ubiquinol, and ubiquinol+geranylgeraniol increased plasma CoQ10; geranylgeraniol alone did not, and patient-reported vitality/health outcomes did not differ from placebo.
rows.evidence_boundary: Biomarker elevation does not by itself demonstrate clinical benefit.

rows.focus: Two-sample Mendelian randomization associated genetically predicted higher omega-3 and lower omega-6/omega-3 ratio with lower Crohn disease susceptibility.
rows.evidence_boundary: Genetically proxied fatty-acid levels are not equivalent to dietary intake or supplementation; heterogeneity makes causality only suggestive.

rows.focus: Cross-sectional collegiate-athlete study found low omega-3 index was common, with only weak correlations with systolic blood pressure and triglycerides.
rows.evidence_boundary: Cross-sectional biomarker associations cannot establish benefit from omega-3 supplementation.

rows.focus: Narrative cardiovascular-diet review emphasized dietary-pattern quality over single nutrients; it also noted dose-dependent coronary benefit signals and atrial-fibrillation concerns with high-dose omega-3 formulations.
rows.evidence_boundary: Narrative synthesis spans heterogeneous evidence and should not be treated as a single intervention estimate.
